name: Sensitive Scalp
description: A hair type characterized by a scalp that is prone to irritation, redness, and discomfort. Individuals with this hair type often experience dry or itchy scalps and may be sensitive to certain ingredients in hair care products.
hair_texture: Varies widely; can range from fine to thick but is more likely to be on the finer side due to potential sensitivity issues that might affect texture
porosity: Moderate to high, as sensitivities often lead to an increased need for moisture retention
characteristics: Can be sensitive to certain ingredients in hair care products
recommended_ingredients: Hydrating agents like hyaluronic acid and glycerin
Anti-inflammatory ingredients such as chamomile, oatmeal, and aloe vera
Natural moisturizers like shea butter and jojoba oil
washing_frequency: 2-3 times per week; avoid over-washing as it can strip the scalp of its natural oils
oil_recommendation: Use light, non-comedogenic oils like coconut or jojoba oil in small amounts for deep conditioning and hair treatment

morning_routine.action: Apply a thin layer of soothing hair serum to the scalp
morning_routine.purpose: Provides immediate relief from any irritation and keeps the scalp hydrated

night_routine.action: Wash hair with a gentle, hydrating shampoo followed by a deep conditioner focused on moisture
night_routine.purpose: Prepares the scalp for overnight repair and hydration while avoiding potential irritants

weekly_care: Deep condition your hair using a mask enriched with soothing ingredients like aloe vera or oatmeal once a week to address dryness and irritation
heat_styling_recommendation: Use heat protectants formulated for sensitive skin, limit heat styling sessions, and cool down hair under running water after using heat tools
lifestyle_tips: Manage stress through relaxation techniques as it can exacerbate scalp sensitivity
Maintain a balanced diet rich in vitamins and minerals that support overall health
common_mistakes: Using harsh chemicals or products that irritate the scalp
Over-washing hair, leading to dryness and more irritation
dont: Do not use overly hot water when washing your hair; it can further irritate a sensitive scalp.
Do not skip the patch test with new products before full application.

seasonal_care.summer: Use lighter, more hydrating products to manage sweat and prevent dryness
seasonal_care.winter: Opt for thicker, richer moisturizers to combat dry winter air
seasonal_care.monsoon: Focus on anti-dandruff products that can help with moisture retention while preventing fungal growth

expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist or trichologist if persistent issues arise, as underlying conditions might need professional attention.
